To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the E/Z-isomerization in guanabanz free base is responsible for the appearance of two solid forms.
we have synthesized, characterized, and reported X-ray crystal structure of two forms (E- and Z-isomers) of guanabenez.

(i) E/Z-isomer is responsible for the formation of two solid forms of guanabenez, (ii) Form I is more stable than the Form II, (iii) the Form II is stabilized by the formation of intermolecular hydrogen bonds, (iv) π-stacking interaction is more in Form II than in Form I, (v) Form I has higher density than the Form II.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure and stability of the two forms of guanabenez free base (E/Z-isomerism).
the synthesis of guanabanz free base and the characterization of two forms, Form I and Form II.
the synthesis and characterization of two new solid forms (geometrical polymorphs) of the drug guanabenz.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the E/Z-isomerization of guanabenez in the solid state leads to the formation of two different solid forms, namely Form I (E-configuration) and Form II.
Form I is the more stable form and the Form II is the metastable form.
the guanabenez free base exists in two different forms in the solid state, which are the E-isomer (Form I) and the Z-isomer (Form II).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a new polymorphic form of guanabanz, which is a pharmaceutical drug.
the two solid forms of guanabenez (Forms I and II) are geometrical polymorph.
we have identified the Z-isomer of guanabenez, which was unknown so far, by using X-ray diffraction, thermochemical analysis and quantum chemical calculations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the guanabenez molecule is a chiral molecule.
the E-isomer of guanabenez is a more stable form than the Z-isomer.
guanabenz exists in two forms in the solid state, and both forms are stable at room temperature.
